newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU said to probe Michelin sales practices.
newsitem.headline: EU said to probe Michelin sales practices.

text.p: The European Commission is probing Europe's biggest tyre maker, Michelin, to see if its sales practices in Europe constitute an abuse of a dominant market position, a Commission source told Reuters on Tuesday.
"There is indeed an investigation under way," the source told Reuters, confirming it concerned the French company.

"Basically, it focuses on the same kinds of behaviour that led the Commission and the Court of Justice at the start of the 1980s to condemn certain practices of this company," the source said, speaking on condition of anonymity.

"We're pursuing the investigation to try to establish the facts, to see if Michelin's practices could constitute an abuse of dominant market position," the source said, noting that no formal complaint had been lodged against Michelin.
An EC document obtained by Reuters said the Commission was studying certain practices in the EU tyre market.
"According to the information that the Commission has, inequitable commercial conditions are allegedly being imposed by a company occupying a dominant position," said the document.
The source confirmed that the Clermont Ferrand-based company was the subject of the letter referring to case "IV/E-2/36.014 Michelin" and a related questionnaire apparently sent to tyre distributors.
The Commission has not made public any probe into Michelin and its spokesman's office did not reply to Reuter enquiries on the case.
A spokesman for Michelin, which vies with Bridgestone as the world's biggest tyre maker, told Reuters: "There is no comment on our part."
Michelin shares, which have rallied strongly this year, closed down 12.1 francs ($2.15) or 3.42 percent in Paris on Tuesday at 341.9 francs per share.
The Commission source said the probe concerned the French market but might involve other European countries.
The questionnaire sought information by February 10 on Michelin's rebate system and other sales practices.
A section on "Michelin's Commercial Policy" asked: "Provide copies of your supply contracts for Michelin tyre since 1985. Are these contracts based on Michelin's usual General Conditions of Sale?"

It then asked: "Do Michelin's General Conditions of Sale establish three categories of rebates (quantity rebates, service quality and rebates determined as a function of efforts to sell new tyres?) How are these rebates calculated? When are they paid? For how long has this system existed?"
It also asked whether other tyre makers employed similar rebate systems.

The source said the case was not related to a proposed joint venture between Michelin and Continental AG of Germany. The EC said in August it proposed to clear the venture once it had sought comment from interested parties. ($ = 5.625 French Francs)
